issue_context.title: Isolate always stops services triggered by other units
issue_context.body:
**systemd version the issue has been seen with**
 > 250, current master

<!-- **NOTE:** Do not submit bug reports about anything but the two most recently released *major* systemd versions upstream! -->
<!--           If there have been multiple stable releases for that major version, please consider updating to a recent one before reporting an issue. -->
<!--           When using a distro package, please make sure that the version reported is meaningful for upstream. -->
<!-- See https://github.com/systemd/systemd-stable/tags for the list of most recent releases. -->
<!-- For older version please use distribution trackers (see https://systemd.io/CONTRIBUTING#filing-issues). -->

**Used distribution**
 > Fedora 34

**Linux kernel version used** (`uname -a`)
<!-- Make sure to enclose the pasted kernel version in `backticks`, so that
     GitHub doesn't convert the `#` character typically included in it into a
     reference to old GitHub issues. -->
 > `5.15.13-100.fc34.x86_64`

**CPU architecture issue was seen on**
 > x86_64

**Expected behaviour you didn't see**
 > A service, triggered by a socket/path/timer, should be handled the same way as the triggering unit by `systemctl isolate`. Specifically, if the triggering unit continues to run in the new target, the service should continue to run too.

**Unexpected behaviour you saw**
 > The service is stopped regardless of the status of the triggering unit.

**Steps to reproduce the problem**
 ```sh
cat >/etc/systemd/system/test.path <<EOF
[Path]
PathModified=/run/test.path

[Install]
WantedBy=paths.target
EOF
cat >/etc/systemd/system/test.service <<EOF
[Service]
Type=simple
ExecStart=/usr/bin/sleep infinity
EOF
systemctl daemon-reload
systemctl enable --now test.path
touch /run/test.path
systemctl isolate multi-user.target
```

**Additional program output to the terminal or log subsystem illustrating the issue**

```text
[root@localhost ~]# systemctl enable --now test.path
Created symlink /etc/systemd/system/paths.target.wants/test.path → ../test.path.
[root@localhost ~]# systemctl is-active test.path test.service
active
inactive
[root@localhost ~]# touch /run/test.path
[root@localhost ~]# systemctl is-active test.path test.service
active
active
[root@localhost ~]# systemctl isolate multi-user.target
[root@localhost ~]# systemctl is-active test.path test.service
active
inactive
```

review_comments: shouldn't this snippet be inside the `shall_stop_on_isolate` helper?

we don't support units that are trigger for other trigger units.

Of course that means we could still do it, except that this then becomes a recursion problem, and we might need to be afraid of cyclic graphs and so on.

hence, let's not even bother, it cannot really happen anyway.
break after this, no need to continue checking

I think this is too simplistic. It only covers units that are one dependency away from a unit that we shall keep. But let's say that we have a unit A which triggers B which requires C. And A is part of the isolation target. When we visit C, we'll schedule a stop job for it.

Don't we need to do a more comprehensive walk where we keep marking units as excluded from isolation walking out further and further into the graph of dependencies?
that sounds correct, but also risky - given this works and is at least a correct but partial fix, maybe it would be better to get this in 253 and then if needed rework later?
